description:
Blocks Enum sort_by/max/max_by/min/min_by/min_max/min_max_by (20 pairs), List.keysort, and the O(n log n) sort-then-group strategy that fz's flat-array Map needs.

VERIFIED at 67e09d373:
  fz:      Enum.sort(["pear", "apple", "fig"])  =>  ["pear", "fig", "apple"]
  Elixir:  Enum.sort(["pear", "apple", "fig"])  =>  ["apple", "fig", "pear"]

It does not error -- it silently produces a wrong ordering. Enum.sort/1 is
'fn (l, r) -> l <= r end', and <, <=, >, >= are numeric-only (ir_interp/binop.rs:21
does as_float().ok_or_else(|| "lhs is not numeric"); native uses IntCC/FloatCC at
prim.rs:1759).

Erlang defines a total order across all terms:
  number < atom < reference < fun < port < pid < tuple < map < list < bitstring

Needs a runtime fz_term_cmp primitive (non-allocating, returns i64) and a decision
about whether <=/< on mixed terms adopt term order or stay numeric-only with a
separate comparison entry point.

comments.text:
fz-5xp.18 leaves you a deletion. Kernel now answers every integer/float pair through a typed clause, and runtime type dispatch selects those clauses even when the static type is a numeric union (verified: operands typed `integer | float` agree with Elixir on all six operators, all three doors). So `lower_cmp_binop`'s coercion slow path in native_codegen/prim.rs -- the both_int tag test, the brif, the box_float_for_any call and the fz_promote_f64 pair -- is no longer reachable for numbers.

What still reaches it is exactly non-numeric operands, which is this ticket's subject and where it currently produces a wrong answer rather than an error (Enum.sort(["pear","apple","fig"]) returns ["pear","fig","apple"]). Whatever term ordering lands here should DELETE that path rather than sit beside it -- a comparison seat that silently promotes a binary to a float is the thing being replaced, not a fallback worth keeping.

fz-5xp.18 advanced this and narrowed what is left.

DONE by fz-5xp.18: numbers order by value across integer/float on all three doors, and BINARIES order byte-lexicographically with the shorter prefix first, so Enum.sort(["pear","apple","fig"]) now returns ["apple","fig","pear"] instead of ["pear","fig","apple"]. Both live in cmp_any_value (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs), the single dynamic ordering that native codegen, the interpreter, guards and the bb intrinsic all call.

WHAT IS LEFT is cross-type order only -- Erlang's number < atom < reference < fun < port < pid < tuple < map < list < bitstring. Verified against Elixir: 1 < "a" is true, :atom < "a" is true, "a" < :atom is false.

It is no longer a silent wrong answer. Kernel declares a clause per orderable pair and NO any/any default, so an unsupported combination is refused at compile time:
    error[spec/violation]: call to  violates its @spec for arguments (:a, :b)
Implementing term order means extending cmp_any_value and adding the Kernel clauses that admit the new pairs -- one place, not two, and the compile error tells you exactly which pair is missing.

fz-5xp.18 advanced this and narrowed what is left.

DONE by fz-5xp.18: numbers order by value across integer/float on all three doors, and BINARIES order byte-lexicographically with the shorter prefix first, so sorting a list of strings now matches Elixir instead of returning them in an arbitrary order. Both live in cmp_any_value (runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs), the single dynamic ordering that native codegen, the interpreter, guards and the bb intrinsic all call.

WHAT IS LEFT is cross-type order only -- Erlang's number, atom, reference, fun, port, pid, tuple, map, list, bitstring sequence. Verified against Elixir: an integer sorts before a binary, and an atom sorts before a binary.

It is no longer a silent wrong answer. Kernel declares a clause per orderable pair and NO any/any default, so an unsupported combination is refused at compile time with a spec/violation naming the operand types. Implementing term order means extending cmp_any_value and adding the Kernel clauses that admit the new pairs -- one place, not two, and the compile error tells you exactly which pair is missing.

title: There is no term ordering: Enum.sort is silently wrong on non-numerics
